== Basis ==
[[File:2BB-2 is a 2BB in-universe..png|thumb|2BB-2 is a 2BB in-universe.]]
2BB is a original droid made for Star Wars: Droid Tycoon. However 2BB does resemble [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/2BB-2 2BB-2] heavily in design. According to Senior ''Star Wars'' Lore Advisor Leland Chee, the various uniquely named BB units, including [[CB]], [[BB9]], and 2BB, are able to be considered as variant models of the main unit. We can speculate that the 2BB's seen from in-game are the base design of 2BB-2 such as how the [[R2]]-series are the base design for [[R2-D2]].

== Trivia ==

* Parts of 2BB are reused for other droids:
** The body of 2BB is reused for the body of [[ZRO-TEC]].
** The entire model of 2BB is reused for the head and body of [[Opti-STRK]] and [[MO-Trak]].
* 2BB is required to create ZRO-TEC with Droid Fusion.
* 2BB counted towards the resistance delivery goals during the [[Events|BB-8 event]].

== Basis ==
[[File:A in-universe A-LT..png|thumb|A in-universe A-LT.]]
A-LT is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a A-LT Utility Droid. Although they were designed as astromech droids, A-LTs were often adapted for more menial tasks such as serving food. A-LT's first appeared in the 2016 film ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/A-LT_Utility_Droid page].

== Trivia ==

* Two A-LT's are required to create [[LOW-MO]] with Droid Fusion.
* Several parts of A-LT can be found around the players workshop.
** TBC
* Parts of A-LT are reused for other droids:
** The wheels of A-LT are reused for the wheels of [[Trak-R]], [[Proto-Roller]], and [[LOW-MO]].
** The body and wheels of A-LT are reused for the body and wheels of Trak-R.
** The head of A-LT is reused for the head of [[DRFT-R]].
*A-LT could be seen in both promo pictures for the Stellar Event.

== Basis ==
[[File:ARG Basis.webp|thumb|ARG19 is an in-universe ARG.]]
ARG is a original droid made for Star Wars Droid Tycoon, however one of such droid with a very simillar design has appeared in-universe. This droid is called ARG19 who first appeared in the 2025 series ''Star Wars: Andor'' in the third episode of the second season called Harvest. We can speculate that the ARG's from in-game are the base design of ARG19 such as how the R2-series are the base design for R2-D2. For more information about ARG19 go to this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/ARG19 page].

== Trivia ==

* Parts of ARG are reused for other droids:
** The wheels of ARG are reused for [[ROLL-R]] and [[WHL-EX]] design.
** The main body of ARG is reused for [[ARM-Core]]'s design.
* ARG is required to create [[WHL-EX]] and [[ARM-Core]] using Droid Fusion.
* A base ARG could be seen at the landing bay next to the cantina during the Fusion Event.

== Basis ==
[[File:B2-RP.png|thumb|A B2 Rocket Trooper in-universe.]]
B2-RP is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. The in-game model does actually not depict the B2-RP as seen in-universe but instead depicts the Super battle droid rocket trooper or simply the B2 Rocket Trooper. The B2 Rocket Trooper was an upgraded variant of the B2-RP battle droid that was built for high-impact assault operations, featuring heavy armor plating alongside shoulder and ankle thrusters that grant superior aerial maneuverability, these droids were used at the end of the Clone Wars.

== Trivia ==

* The model of B2-RP actually depicts the B2 super rocket trooper. The name "B2-RP"  is a separate B2-series super battle droid variant in-universe.
* B2-RP is required to create [[ORB-XL]] with Droid Fusion.
* Parts of B2-RP model are reused for other droids:
** The entire model of B2-RP is reused for the body of [[Haul-R]].
** B2-RP's jetpacks, legs, and arms are reused for the jetpack, legs, and arms of [[ORB-XL]].

== Basis ==
[[File:BB-8 Basis.png|thumb|BB-8 was a BB in-universe.]]
BB's were droid in the Star Wars universe. In universe these droid are called BB-series astromech droids. These droids featured a spherical body that allowed the droid to roll in any direction, with a head usually atop the body but not meant to be permanently physically attached to it. The BB droids first appeared in the 2015 movie ''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/BB-series_astromech_droid page].

== Trivia ==

* Several BB's and BB parts can be found around the world:
** A BB is used to promote the VIP pack in the upper cantina shop.
** The body of a BB can be found on top of the crafting station in the shipyard.
** A beskar BB could be seen on the landing bay during the Beskar event.
* BB is required to create [[N-UL]] using Droid Fusion.
** N-UL also reuses the head of BB for it's own head.
* [[BB8|BB-8]] shares the same model as BB.
* BB counted towards the resistance delivery goals during the [[Events|BB-8 event]].

{{PrevNext|currentsize=50px|previmg=D-O Main0.png|prev=D-O|prevsize=40px|currentimg=BB-8 Main.png|next=CB-23|nextimg=CB-23 Main.png|nextsize=50px}}{{Droid Infobox Official|Name='''{{PAGENAME}}'''|rarity=Iconic|class=Astromech|companion_ability=2x Upgrade Chips|released=v1.06 (6/5/2026)|image1=BB-8 Main.png}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} astromech droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Methods ==
{{PAGENAME}} can be obtained for free after compleating the tutorial <small>(starting from 7/11/2026).</small> BB-8 can also be obtained during events and at the [[Nova Shop]].

* BB-8 could be obtained for free after delivering 10 BB's to Poe Dameron during the BB-8 event.
* BB-8 could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 60 Treats at the Event Shop (purchase the costume to obtain).
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Ability & Trait ==
When BB-8 is active as the player's companion, all Upgrade Chips obtained are doubled. This bonus applies to:

* World pickups
* Selling droid variants
* Crates (from world quests)
* Daily Tasks
* Cantina Missions
* Scrap Station
* Upgrade Chip Station
* Super Crates
* CB-23's Mission
* Events 
For example, if the player has a BB-8 as companion and picks up 100 Upgrade Chips from a World Quest, they receive an additional 100 Upgrade Chips.

=== Trait: Upgrade Chip Master ===
<small>''Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''</small>

BB-8's Iconic trait is called '''Upgrade Chip Master'''. This trait allows his companion ability to remain active even while he is working in the players base. This means that you always can pick up 2x Upgdrade Chips without having BB-8 as your companion. However, BB-8 must be actively working in your base for the trait to take effect.

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''15%''' of the players total base income. 

== Basis ==
[[File:BB-8 Basis.png|thumb|BB-8 as seen in-universe.]]
BB-8 was a loyal, spherical astromech droid with a free-moving dome head who served Resistance pilot Poe Dameron, playing a pivotal role in delivering the map to Luke Skywalker and aiding the Resistance against the First Order. BB-8 first appeared in the 2015 film ''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'' as one of the main characters. For more information about BB-8 check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/BB-8 page].

== Trivia ==

* BB-8 was the first Iconic droids introduced to the game. 
* BB-8 was first classed as a Mythic droid, this was later changed to Iconic.
* BB-8 companion perk was changed from a 100% Upgrade Chip pickup from crates to 2x Upgrade Chips.
* BB-8 shares the same model as [[BB]].
* BB-8 could be seen in the very first trailer for Droid Tycoon.

== Basis ==
[[File:BB9 Basis .jpg|thumb|BB-9E is a in-universe BB9.]]
BB9 is a original droid in the Star Wars universe. However BB9 does resemble BB-9E heavily in design. According to Senior ''Star Wars'' Lore Advisor Leland Chee, the various uniquely named BB units, including [[CB]], BB9, and [[2BB]], are able to be considered as variant models of the main unit. We can speculate that the BB9's from in-game are the base design of BB-9E such as how the [[R2]]-series are the base design for [[R2-D2]].

== Trivia ==

* In the cantina, a BB9 can be found called Boss BB9. 
* BB9 is the earliest required {{Official:Rarity|Legendary}} droid in the rebirth system. In Path 1, it is needed for Rebirth 11 rather than the standard Rebirth 12 or 13.
* BB9 is the first {{Official:Rarity|Legendary}} droid to be somewhat based on a actual droid in the Star Wars universe.
* BB9 is required to create [[RO-TOR]] and [[QIK-BIT]] with Droid Fusion.
* Parts of BB9 are reused for other droids:
** BB9's entire model is reused for [[QIK-BIT]] and the head and body of [[Strike-Orb]].
** BB9's body is reused for the body of [[RO-TOR]].

== Basis ==
[[File:BDX Explorer Basis.png|thumb|A in-universe BDX Explorer.]]
The BDX Explorer is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a BDX droids but it's also reffered to as BDX explorer droids. These droids were employed for gathering information, such as mapping terrain, geographic analysis, and scanning objects and structures. These droids could be first seen in real-life at ''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge theme land in Disneyland in California.

== Trivia ==

* BDX Explorer is the cheapest {{Official:Rarity|Rare}} droid currently in the game.
* BDX Explorer was the first droid shown in the release trailer for Star Wars: Droid Tycoon.
* BDX Explorer is required to create [[BTL-R]] and [[AXI-POD]] with Droid Fusion.
* Parts of BDX Explorer are reused for other droids:
** BDX Explorers head are reused for the heads of [[BAL-Core]] and [[Proto-Roller]].
** BDX Explorers legs are reused for the legs of [[BAL-Core]] and [[Sen-Tri]].
** BDX Explorers body is reused for the main body of [[BTL-R]], [[Sen-Tri]], [[Proto-Roller]], and [[AXI-POD]].
* Several BDX Explorers can be found around the world:
** Two BDX Explorers can be found near the matchmaking portal at the cantina.
** A blue BDX Explorer can be found near the pickaxe forge area of the cantina.
** A {{Variant|Gold}} BDX Explorer can be found on top of some pipes near the Droid Upgrade area of the cantina.
** A pink BDX Explorer can be found at the Cantina Shop area of the cantina standing above the Companion Pack.
** A BDX Explorer could be seen near the landing dock during the DJ R-3X event.
* Several heads of the BDX Explorer can be seen hanging from the ceiling at the main workers area of the players workshop and on top of the workers crafting bench.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} protocol droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Methods ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* C-3PO could be obtained for free after fishing up all 7 C-3PO parts during the C-3PO event and C-3PO event re-run.
* {{PAGENAME}} could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 100 Treats at the Event Shop (purchase the costume to obtain).
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''200 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Ability & Traits ==
When C-3PO is active as the player's companion, crafted droid that are sold will reward the player with '''2x Credits'''.

==== Event Benefits ====
If C-3PO was the players companion during the C-3PO event, the player would have a additional benefit:

* The player earns bonus credits and upgrade chips after selling scrap.

=== Trait: Droid Sell Master ===
''<small>Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.</small>''

C-3PO's iconic trait is called Droid Sell Master. This trait allows his companion ability to remain active even while he is working in the players base. This means players can earn 2x Credits after selling droids. However, C-3PO must be actively working in the players base for the trait to take effect.

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''25%''' of the players total base income. 

== Basis ==
[[File:C-3PO basis.jpg|thumb|C-3PO as seen in-universe.]]
C-3PO is a well known droid in the Star Wars Universe. C-3PO is a 3PO-series protocol droid fluent in over six million forms of communication, built from spare parts by Anakin Skywalker on Tatooine to assist in human-cyborg relations before becoming a faithful companion to R2-D2 throughout major galactic conflicts. C-3PO first appeared in the 1977 film ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'' as one of the main characters. For more information about C-3PO check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/C-3PO page].

== Trivia ==

* C-3PO is the first and currently only droid that has switched it's class. Prior to v1.30, C-3PO was classed as a worker droid but with the introduction of protocol droids, C-3PO was switched to be classed correctly.
* C-3PO was first teased at end of the R2-D2 event. R2-D2 also mentiones C-3PO during the event.
* C-3PO could be seen leading several protocol droids at the end of the D-O event.
* C-3PO along with [[R2-D2]] generate the most % of income.
* C-3PO and R2-D2 are the most expensive Iconic droids that can be purchased at the Nova Shop besides [[CB-23]].

== Rebirth Requirements ==
CB is required for the following [[Rebirths|rebirth]] requirements:

* '''Path 1'''
** {{Variant|Base}} CB is required for Rebirth 1.

== Basis ==
[[File:CB-23 Basis.webp|thumb|CB inspired basis in universe.]]
CB is a original droid for Star Wars: Droid Tycoon. However CB does resemble [[CB-23]] heavily in design. According to Senior ''Star Wars'' Lore Advisor Leland Chee, the various uniquely named BB units, including CB, [[BB9]], and [[2BB]], are able to be considered as variant models of the main unit. We can speculate that the CB's from in-game are the base design of CB-23 such as how the R2-series are the base design for R2-D2.

== Trivia ==

* A {{Variant|Gold}} CB can be found on a crate at the Droid Upgrade area of the cantina.
* CB is required to create [[ORB-XL]] with Droid Fusion.
** ORB-XL also reuses the body of CB for it's own body.
* CB shares the same model with [[CB-23]].
* CB shares the same body with BB, CB-23 and BB-8. The body is also re-used in the design of Orb-Walker.
* CB share the same cost, income, sell price, companion perk and crafting time for all it's rarity's with [[R3]] and [[R5]].
* CB counted towards the resistance delivery goals during the [[Events|BB-8 event]].
* Several CB's were located at the current SRB area instead of the two RIC-1200's. These were later removed in an update leading to the introduction of Super Rebirth.

== Obtaining Methods ==
CB-23 is obtainable in the Nova Shop but could also be obtained in events:

* CB-23 could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 80 Treats at the Event Shop (purchase the costume to obtain).
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''250''' '''Nova Crystals'''

== Companion Ability & Trait ==
[[File:CB-23 Secret Mission.png|left|thumb|CB-23 Mission Rewards]]When CB-23 is placed in an astromech mission slot, she unlocks a special mission with the following rewards:

* '''90% chance:''' Upgrade Chips
* '''10% chance:''' 40 or 80 Nova Crystals


=== Trait: Hyperdrive ===
<small>''Icconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''</small>

CB-23's iconic trait is called '''World Mission Master'''. This trait triples the amount of Upgrade Chip and Nova Crystal obtained from CB-23's astromech mission.

== Income ==
CB-23 generates '''15%''' of the players total base income.

== Basis ==
[[File:CB-23 Basis.webp|thumb|CB-23 as seen in-universe.]]
CB-23 was a droid in the Star Wars Universe. CB-23 was a red-and-teal CB-series astromech droid who temporarily served Kazuda Xiono on the Colossus station before stepping in as Poe Dameron's co-pilot during BB-8's absence. CB-23 first appeared in the seventh episode of the first season of ''Star Wars Resistance'' called ''Signal from Sector Six'' which premiered in 2018. For more information about [[CB-23]] basis check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/CB-23 page].

== Trivia ==

* CB-23 is currently the only {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} droid in the game to be not released in a event. CB-23 was first added as part of the introduction to Super Rebirth.
* CB-23 is the most expensive {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} droid costing 75 Nova Crystals compared to R2-D2 and C-3PO that cost 60 Nova Crystals.
* CB-23 shares the same model as [[CB]].
* CB-23 mission rewards has changed over the time:
** The mission was first buffed to contain double the rewards.
** The mission was later buffed again to contain double rewards.
* CB-23's mission was originally called Mythic Missions, but it was later left unnamed since it does not reward any Mythic droids.

== Obtaining Methods ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* {{PAGENAME}} could be obtained after earning 75 Junk Points during the Chopper event and the Chopper re-run event.
* {{PAGENAME}} (and it's costume) could have been obtained after earning 75 Pumpkin Points during the Pumpkin Smash event.
* Chopper (and it's costume) could have been purchased at the Gonk-O-Ween Shop for 80 treats.
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Perk & Trait ==
When Chopper is the players companion, the player receives a +50% Crit Chance and a +50% Crit Damage during droid crafting. This can be stacked with the Crit Chance, Crit Damage and Multi-Crit Upgrades that can be bought at the Nova Shop. The amount of Crit Damage depends on the players pickaxe level.

=== Trait: Crit Expert ===
''Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''

DJ R-3X's trait is called '''Crit Expert'''. If Chopper is equipped as a companion, the player receives +1 stage of Multi Crit. This stacks with the Multi Crit upgrade at the [[Nova Shop]].

== Basis ==
[[File:Chopper Basis.png|thumb|Chopper as seen in-universe.]]
Chopper is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. Chopper also known as C1-10P is a cantankerous C1-series astromech droid and loyal ''Ghost'' crew mechanic who fought the Empire alongside Hera Syndulla's Rebels despite his notoriously fiery personality. Chopper first appeared in a storybook called ''Chopper Saves the Day'' which was released in 2014 to tie in with the tv series called ''Star Wars: Rebels'' which released the same year. For more information about Chopper check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/C1-10P page].

== Trivia ==

* Chopper has an unique droid sound effect.
* Chopper is one of the two droids with a [[List of Cosmetics|hat]]. The other being Mister Bones.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} worker droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Methods ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can currently be purchased at the Nova Shop.

* D-O could be obtained for free after earning 400 Trust Points during the D-O event and the D-O re-run event.
* D-O can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Ability & Trait ==
When D-O is active as the player's companion, the crafting time for droids in the fusion tank is reduced by half after hitting the tank with your pickaxe. 

=== Trait: Fusion Master ===
<small>''Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''</small>

D-O's Iconic trait is called '''Fusion Master'''. This trait allows his companion ability to remain active even while he is working in the players base. This means players can automatically half the total fusion crafting time without having D-O equipped as companion. However, D-O must be actively working in the players base for the trait to take effect.

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''15%''' of the players total base income. 

== Basis ==
[[File:D-O Basis.png|thumb|D-O as seen in-universe.]]
D-O is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. D-O was a timid, single-wheeled custom droid who was reactivated by BB-8 on Pasaana and later went on to aid the Resistance with critical information about the Sith Eternal. D-O first appeared in the 2019 film ''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker''. For more information about D-O check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/D-O page].

== Trivia ==

* D-O was first supposed to release after the Chopper Event, this was later delayed for the release of Stellar and Droid Fusion.
* The D-O companion perk originally required players to have D-O equipped before pressing the fuse button to apply the half fusion time bonus; this was later changed so the modifier applies automatically whenever a player pickaxes the fusion tank while D-O is active.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} worker droid in Droid Tycoon. 

== Obtaining Methods ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* DJ R-3X could be obtained for free after helping with the construction of 10 parties during the DJ R-3X event and DJ R-3X event re-run.
* {{PAGENAME}} could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 800 V-Bucks at the Event Shop (purchase the bundle to obtain).
* DJ R-3X can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Ability & Traits ==
DJ R-3X has two different abilities:

When DJ R-3X is active as the player's companion, the player earns '''double rewards''' from any crate in the world. This ability applies to:

* Regular crates found around the world.
* Super Crates

<small>''Note: Crates awarded from Astromech and World (Scourge) missions do '''not''' receive double rewards.''</small>

Additionally, DJ R-3X earns '''2x points during World Missions''', making reaching 1-2-3-4 stars much more easy.

==== Event Benefits ====
If DJ R-3X was the players companion during the DJ R-3X event, the player would earn 3 benefits:

* All different type of crates could be opend.
* Crates with stage equipment would open in a instant without having to wait.
* Delivering crates would reward the player with 2x Credits.

=== Trait: World Mission Master ===
<small>''Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''</small>

DJ R-3X's iconic trait is called '''World Mission Master'''. This trait allows his companion ability to remain active even while he is working in the players base. This means players can earn 2x World Mission Points and receive 2x crate rewards without having DJ R-3X equipped as their companion. However, DJ R-3X must be actively working in the players base for the trait to take effect.

== Income ==
DJ R-3X generates '''15%''' of the players total base income. 

== Basis ==
[[File:DJ R-3X Basis.jpg|thumb|DJ R-3X as seen in ''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge.]]
DJ R-3X is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. In universe this droid was called R-3X or simply Rex. R-3X was an RX-series pilot droid who functioned as a pilot before being reprogrammed into a DJ on Batuu. The DJ was first created for a simulator ride theme park attraction located at Disneyland called ''Star Tours'' that first opend in 1987. In the current canon, DJ R-3X first appeared in the third episode of the first season of ''Star Wars: Rebels'' called Droids in Distress that released in 2014. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R-3X page].

== Trivia ==

* With the introduction of the new World Mission system in v1.30, DJ R-3X's companion ability was changed to better fit the new system. His old companion ability allowed players to complete all three types of World Missions without having to switch to the required class.
* DJ R-3X was the first Iconic worker to be released in Droid Tycoon.
* DJ R-3X can be seen at the cantina behind the bar.

The DRK-1 Probe is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid or Sith probe droid. This droid was capable of tracking targets quietly and it was thus used by the Galactic Empire and even the Sith. The DRK-1 Probe first appeared in the 1999 movie ''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''The Phantom Menace''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/DRK-1_Dark_Eye_probe_droid page].

== Basis ==
[[File:Gonk Basis.webp|thumb|An in-universe Gonk.]]
The Gonk is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. Altough being called Gonk, the droid model in-game resembles the EG-series power droid instead of the suggested GNK-series power droids. Altough being different, both of these power droid that were often referred to as gonk droids in imitation of their honking sound. The Gonk first appeared in the 1977 movie ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/EG-series_power_droid page]. 

== Trivia ==

* The Gonk is required to create [[SCRP-R]] and [[X-ONK]] with Droid Fusion.
* Parts of Gonk are reused for other droids:
** Gonk's body is reused for the body of [[AMP Walker]] and [[X-ONK]].
** Gonk's legs are reused for the legs of [[Opti-Pod]] and [[SCRP-R]].
* The Gonk was one of the many Gonk droids that could be given to WG-22 during the Iconic Gonk event.
* The Gonk has the same stats as [[R8]] with the only difference being the companion perk.
* The Gonk's body can be seen in several locations:
** It can be seen at the Scrap Table.
** It can be seen on a little conveyor at the workers slot between te lounge and battle area.
** It can be seen on top of the workers crafting bench.
* The Gonk can be seen in several locations around the map:
** A purple Gonk can be seen fixing a pillar besides the barbeque behind the landing dock.
** A black Gonk can be seen fixing a power engine at the Sandcrawler.
** A grey Gonk can be found at the front of the cantina next to a B1-Battle. The player can talk to this Gonk and it will say two things: <nowiki>''</nowiki>Gonk! Translation: Gonk!<nowiki>''</nowiki> or <nowiki>''</nowiki>Gonk. Gonk, Gonk! Translation: Gonk is good at fixing broken things around town!<nowiki>''</nowiki>
** A cyan Gink can be found fixing something in the cantina next to the Lucky Pit.
** A very hidden white Gonk can be found in a little ravine behind a large sand building with pipes coming out of it. It's located near the end of the orange/black jetpack rings. You will need a jetpack to find this Gonk.
** A Beskar Gonk could be seen on the landing dock during the Beskar Event.
** A Gonk could be seen dancing on the stage during the DJ R-3X event.
** A Galactic Gonk could be seen in the first Galactic teaser at the end of the C-3PO event.
* A Gonk blueprint can be seen on the logo of the Sell Blueprint vendor. Another Gonk blueprint can be seen held by a Jawa at the Starter Pack area of the Upper Cantina Shop.
* A tipped over brown Gonk could have been found at a moisture vaporator (white tower) near the end of orange/black jetpack rings. This was removed with the introduction of the new World Quest.
* A red Gonk can be seen fixing a moisture vaporator (white tower) near the start of the Sandcrawler conveyor, this was removed during the Gonk-O-Ween event.
* A Gonk could have been seen on a banner of the Companion Pack behind the pink BDX Explorer at the Upper Cantina Shop. This was later removed in a unknown update.

== Basis ==
[[File:B2ESMO Basis.png|thumb|B2EMO is a Groundmech in-universe,]]
Groundmech is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In-universe these droids are called B2 groundmechs. These droids were intended for use in salvage operations and as such were equipped with many tools to assist human operators. Groundmech first appeared in the first season of ''Star Wars: Andor'' in the first episode dubbed ''Kassa'' that released in 2022. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/B2_groundmech page].

== Trivia ==

* Parts of Groundmech are reused for the other droids:
** The head/top part of Groundmech is reused for the head of [[Trak-R]].
** The top part of the body of Groundmech is reused for the body of [[SCRP-R]].
** The wheels of Groundmech is resued for the wheels of [[QIK-BIT]].
* Groudmech is required to create [[SCRP-R]] and [[QIK-BIT]] using Droid Fusion.
* A Mythic/Iconic Groundmech blueprint can be seen hidden at the blueprint vendor. This is most likely a hint for a future release of B2EMO.
* A Groundmech could have been seen in a banner behind the pink BDX Explorer at the upper cantina shop area. This was later removed.
* A Scourge {{PAGENAME}} can be seen next to Scourge Prime at the Scourge area of the world.
* A Beskar Groundmech could be seen at the landing dock during the Beskar Event.
*

[[File:Gunrunner Basis.png|thumb|A in-universe Gunrunner.]]
Gunrunner is a droid in the Star Wars universe. As a relatively new addition to the franchise, information about these droids remains limited. Gunrunners were designed to operate spacecraft, particularly for transporting valuable or high-risk cargo and passengers. They made their first appearance in the 2026 film ''Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu''.

== Trivia ==

* Gunrunner is required to create [[N-UL]] and [[ORB-XL]] with Droid Fusion.
** N-UL also reuses the body of Gunrunner for it's own body.
* Parts of Gunrunner are reused for other droids:
** The body of Gunrunner is reused for the body of [[N-UL]].
** The head of Gunrunner is reused for the ehad of [[ORB-XL]].
* Gunrunner was released to promote the movie ''Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu''.
* Gunrunner is currently the only droid that isn't a fusion or Iconic droid to be released after the release of the game.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} battle droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Method ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* {{PAGENAME}} could be obtained for free after delivering 15 Beskar crates during The Mandalorian event.
* {{PAGENAME}} could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 80 Treats at the Event Shop (purchase the costume to obtain).
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Perk & Trait ==
When IG-11 Marshal is equipped as a companion, the player gains an indestructible shield whenever they hold a blueprint. This effect is similar to the shield granted after purchasing a blueprint from the Limited Offer shop. This perk is especially useful in public lobbies to protect players from being eliminated while carrying rare blueprints.

=== Trait: Blueprint Protector ===
''<small>Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.</small>''

IG-11 Marshal's iconic trait is called '''Blueprint Protector'''. While IG-11 Marshal is equipped as a companion, all blueprints you pick up become unpickable for other players, preventing them from being stolen. If you remove IG-11 Marshal from your companion slot, these blueprints become pickable for other players again.

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''15%''' of the players total base income. 

== In-Universe ==
[[File:IG-11 Marshal Basis.webp|thumb|IG-11 Marshal as seen in-universe.]]
IG-11 Marshal or simply IG-11 is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. Reprogrammed from a cold-blooded bounty hunter into a devoted caregiver, IG-11 sacrificed himself to protect Grogu, later serving as the rebuilt exoskeleton IG-12 controlled by the young foundling, before ultimately being restored to become the Marshal of Nevarro City. IG-11 first appeared in the first episode of the first season of ''The Mandalorian'' called ''Chapter 1: The Mandalorian'' that first aired in 2019. For more information about IG-11 check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/IG-11 page].

== Trivia ==

* IG-11 Marshal was released to help promote the movie: The Mandalorian and Grogu.
* IG-11 Marshal model is shared with [[IG]].

[[File:Imperial Probe Basis.webp|thumb|166x166px|An in-universe Imperial Probe.]]
The Imperial Probe is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a Viper probe droid but it's commonly referred to as the Imperial probe droid. These droids were used by the Galactic Empire for deep space exploration and reconnaissance. The Imperial Probe first appeared in the 1980 film ''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back''. * Parts of the Imperial Probe are reused for other droids:
** The main body of the Imperial Probe (and the legs) are reused for the main body of [[NAV-EX]].
** The top part of the head of the Imperial Probe is reused for the head of [[Opti-Pod]].
* The head of the Imperial Probe can be found in two locations of the players workshop.
** The lower part of the head can be found on the conveyor of the workers area between the lounge and battle area.
** The top and lower parts can be found on top of the battle crafting bench.
* A Scourge Imperial Porbe can be seen next to Scourge Prime at the Socurge area of the world.

For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/LEP-series_service_droid page].

== Trivia ==

* LEP is the only droid that does not show it's full body on the blueprint art.

[[File:Loadlifter Basis.jpg|thumb|An in-universe Loadlifter.]]
Loadlifters were droid in the Star Wars Universe. These droids were a model of loader droid droids programmed for carrying their masters' cargo. The design in-game resembles the Loadlifter called HURID-327. These droids first appeared in the 2016 mobile game ''Star Wars Rebels: Recon Missions''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Loadlifter_droid_(model) page].

* Loadlifter is holding a black crate in his blueprint art.
* Loadlifter is required to create [[LUG-G]] and [[LOW-MO]] with Droid Fusion.
** LUG-G reuses the arms and legs of Loadlifter for it's own arms and legs.
** LOW-MO reuses the head of Loadlifter for it's own head.
* A Loadlifter can be found at the SRB area of the cantina, being the vendor of the Return Iconic Droid shop.

LOM is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. In-universe these droids are called LOM-series protocol droids. Designed with insectile features, LOM-series protocol droids were a market failure that frequently suffered from software flaws, causing many to abandon protocol work and become Outer Rim bounty hunters or enforcers. LOM first appeared in the 1980 movie ''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/LOM-series_protocol_droid page].

== Trivia ==

{{PrevNext|currentsize=50px|previmg=Chopper Main.png|prev=Chopper|prevsize=50px|currentimg=Mister Bones Main.png|next=IG-11 Marshal|nextimg=IG-11 Marshall Main.png|nextsize=50px}}{{Droid Infobox Official|Name='''{{PAGENAME}}'''|rarity=Iconic|class=Battle|companion_ability=2x Damage & Credits from eliminating NPC's|released=v1.19 (28/6/2026)|image1=Mister Bones Main.png}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} battle droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Method ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* {{PAGENAME}} could be obtained for free after eliminating 100 Storm Troopers during the Mister Bones event.
* {{PAGENAME}} could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 80 Treats at the Event Shop (purchase the costume to obtain).
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Perk & Trait ==
Mister Bones has two companion perks along with one secret perk. He deals 2x damage against players and NPCs during world missions, and his second companion perk helps players earn credits after defeating an NPC. Mister Bones will not earn credits after defeating a real player.

=== Trait: Lifesteal ===
''Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''

Mister Bones' iconic trait is called '''Life Steal'''. This trait allows the player to regain 20% of their max health after defeating an enemy NPC. Mister Bones must be your companion for this trait to work.

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''15%''' of the players total base income. 

== Basis ==
[[File:Mister Bones Basis.jpg|thumb|Mister Bones as seen in a novel.]]
Mister Bones is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. Mister Bones is a heavily modified B1 battle droid, custom-built by Temmin Wexley on Akiva to act as a fiercely protective, acrobatics-trained bodyguard. He had a sadistic personality and would sing or hum while attacking and maiming his victims. Mister Bones first appeared in the novel called Aftermath which was released in 2015. For more information about Mister Bones check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mister_Bones page].

== Trivia ==

* Mister Bones has a unqiue sound effect if the player opens his droid menu.
* Mister Bones could be first seen locked away in the crashed AT-AT after the BB-8 event. This was a teaser to his event.
* Mister Bones is one of the two droid with a unique hat. The other being [[Chopper]].
* Mister Bones has two working animations. If placed on a battle slot, Mister Bones will be standing and shooting. If he is placed in an Worker or Astromech slot, he will be on his knees fixing something.

== Basis ==
[[File:Mouse Basis.webp|thumb|A in-universe Mouse Droid.]]
The Mouse is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a '''MSE-6 series repair droid''', also known as a mouse droid. The Mouse was a tiny, wheel-based messenger droids that zip through the corridors of Imperial bases delivering messages and performing routine maintenance tasks. The Mouse first appeared in the 1977 film ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/MSE-6_series_repair_droid page]. 

== Trivia ==

* The common Mouse is the cheapest droid you buy at the Sandcrawler. 
* Mouse is required to create [[WHL-EX]] using Droid Fusion.
* Parts of Mouse are reused for other droids:
** The main body of Mouse is reused for [[WHL-EX]] and [[Mecha-Droid]].
* Mouse is a potential Trade Requirement in the cantina.
* The player can find several Mouse's in the world:
** Next to the Cantina and behind the Docking Bay, players can find a black mouse droid wearing a yellow cap, cooking meat. Interacting with the mouse gives the player a meat consumable.
** There are two additional black mouse droids at the Sandcrawler. Both are equipped with blowtorches and appear to be repairing the conveyor belt.

MPH is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. In-universe they are called MPH power droids. These power droids were used as ambulatory batteries to recharge vehicles and machinery. They could be seen working in spice mines but also at docking bay's. The MPHs first appeared in the 2018 movie ''Solo: A Star Wars Story''. == Basis ==
[[File:Pit Basis.jpg|thumb|Three in-universe Pit Droids.]]
The Pit is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a DUM-series pit droid. These little and fearless repair droids first appeared in the 1999 film ''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/DUM-series_pit_droid page].

== Trivia ==

* Altough being more expensive than the Mouse, Pit and Mouse share the same base income, making Mouse more affordable for very early game.
* The Pit can sometimes be a trade request in the cantina.
* Pit is required to create [[RO-TOR]] with droid fusion.
* Parts of the Pit are reused for other droids:
** Pit's head is reused for the head of [[Vect-Arm]] and [[Cyclo-Grav]].
** Pit's arms and legs are reused for the arms and legs of [[Mecha-Droid]] and [[RO-TOR]].
** Pit's entire body is reused for the body of [[Mono-WLKR]].
* There are two Pit's found around the open-world:
** The Lucky Pit found in the cantina is a Pit Droid.
** There is a Pit droid found fixing a vent above the tavern of the cantina.
** There was a {{Variant|Beskar}} Pit droid fixing the blueprint storage in the SRB shop area. This was removed in an unknown update.
** There were two dancing Pit droids on the stage during the DJ R-3X Event.
* A Pit<nowiki>'s ''head''</nowiki> can be found in several locations in the players workshop:
** One can be found on the workers crafting bench.
** One can be found at the main workers area.
** One can be found hanging from the ceiling at the main workers area.
** One can be found on the little conveyor on the workers slot between te lounge and battle area.
** A gray head can be found on a cabinet next to the scrap station.
* Several other parts of the Pit such as the arms and legs can be seen hanging from the ceiling at the main workers area of the players workshop.
* A yellow Pit can be seen on a computer at the workers slot between te lounge and battle area.

PLNKs first appeared in the third epiosde of the first season ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' called ''Shadow of Malevolence'' that first aired in 2008. == Basis ==
[[File:R2 Basis.png|thumb|A in-universe R2.]]
R2's were droid in the Star Wars universe. In universe these droid are called the R2-series astromech droids. The R2-series were the most popular line of all the R-series. They sported a distinctive domed head and were programmed to perform a variety of tasks. The R2's first appeared in the 1977 film ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R2-series_astromech_droid page].

== Trivia ==

* Parts of R2 are reused for other droids:
** The legs of a R2 are reused for the legs of [[AMP Walker]] and [[MO-Trak]].
** The head and body of a R2 is reused for the body of [[OPT-AR]].
** The bodyand legs of R2 is reused for the body of [[R3]], [[R4]], [[R5]], [[R6]], [[R8]], and [[R9]].
* Two R2's are required to create [[OPT-AR]] with [[Droid Fusion]].
* Parts of R2 can be found in the players workshop:
** A R2 head and legs can be found in the main workers area of the players workshop.
** A R2 head can be found hanging in the main workers area of the players workshop.
** A R2 head and body can be found on the conveyor in the second workers area between the lounge and firing range.
** A R2 head can be found on top of the crafting station in the shipyard.
* A R2 could be seen near the landing bay next to the cantina during the DJ R-3X event.
* R2-D2 reuses the same model as R2.
* All R-series astromech droids except [[R7]] reuses the same body/legs as R2.
* A unknown upcoming Iconic droid will share the same model for R2.

{{PrevNext|currentsize=50px|previmg=CB-23 Main.png|prev=CB-23|prevsize=50px|currentimg=R2-D2 Main.png|next=Chopper|nextimg=Chopper Main.png|nextsize=50px}}{{Droid Infobox Official|Name='''{{PAGENAME}}'''|rarity=Iconic|class=Astromech|companion_ability=Double Astromech Mission Rewards|released=v1.19 (28/6/2026)|image1=R2-D2 Main.png}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} astromech droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Methods ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* {{PAGENAME}} could be obtained for free after obtaining 600 Data Chips during the R2-D2 event and the R2-D2 re-run event.
* {{PAGENAME}} could be purchased from the Gonk-O-Ween event for 100 Treats at the Event Shop (purchase the costume to obtain).
* {{PAGENAME}} can be purchased at the Nova Shop for '''200 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Perk & Trait ==
When R2-D2 is placed in an astromech mission slot, an additional crate spawns once the mission is completed. This means that the player can earns double the reward from one single astromech mission.

=== Trait: Double Crate Chance ===
<small>''Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.''</small>

R2-D2's Iconic trait is called '''Double Crate Chance'''. This trait gives every astromech mission a 50% chance to give two crates after compleation instead of one. This includes CB-23's mission. R2-D2 still receives it's usual two crates with 100%. However, R2-D2 must be actively working in the players base for the trait to take effect.

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''25%''' of the players total base income. 

== Basis ==
[[File:R2-D2 Basis.png|thumb|R2-D2 as seen in-universe.]]
R2-D2 is a well known droid in the Star Wars Universe. R2-D2 is an [[R2]]-series astromech droid known for his resourcefulness and brave nature, serving as a skilled starship mechanic, computer interface specialist, and loyal companion to Anakin Skywalker, Ahsoka Tano, and Luke Skywalker. R2-D2 first appeared in the 1977 film ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'' as one of the main characters. For more information about R2-D2 check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R2-D2 page].

== Trivia ==

* R2-D2 model is shared with the regular [[R2]] series droid.
* R2-D2 along with C-3PO generate the most % of income.
* R2-D2 and CB-23 are the only two droids currently in the game with a companion perk that doesn't require them to be active as the player's companion.
* R2-D2 and C-3PO are the most expensive Iconic droids that can be purchased at the Nova Shop besides [[CB-23]].
* R2-D2 perk was changed from making astromech missions shorter if R2-D2 was the players companion to double astromech rewards.
* R2-D2 could be first seen in the first trailer for Droid Tycoon.

== Basis ==
[[File:R3 Basis.webp|thumb|The in-universe R3.]]
R3 is a real droid in the Star Wars universe. In univere it's called a R3-series astromech droid. R3 astromechs had faster processing abilities than the more common R2 units. They first appeared in the 1977 film ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R3-series_astromech_droid page]. 

== Trivia ==

* The design of R3 is nearly identical to [[R2]]'s design. The only differences in design (besides the customizations options) is that the head is slightly transparent (cable visible on the back of it's head). The R3 seen on a blueprint actually has a more transparent head. However in-game the head is nearly solid making it identical to the R2's.
* A R3 can be found in the cantina.
* Several R3 blueprints can be found around the Sell Blueprint vendor.
* R3 shares the same cost, income, sell price, companion perk and crafting time for all it's rarity's with [[CB]] and [[R5]].

RIC is a droid in the Star Wars universe. In-universe these droids are called RIC-series general labor droid. RIC was a single wheeled labor droid designed for urban transport, programmed to pull passenger cabs through busy city streets like Mos Espa. RIC's first appeared in the 2002 movie ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones''. For more information around the basis check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/RIC-series_general_labor_droid page].

== Trivia ==

* The Hat shop at the cantina is carried by a RIC.
* RIC is required to create [[RIV-3T]] and [[AXI-POD]] with Droid Fusion.
* Parts of RIC are reused for other droids:
** RIC's arms and wheel is reused for the arm and wheels of [[RIV-3T]].
** RIC's entire body is reused for the body of [[DRFT-R]].
** RIC's head is reused for the head of [[AXI-POD]].
* [[RIC-1200]] reuses some elements of RIC such as the wheel.

RIC-1200 first appeared in the fifteenth episode of the fifth season of ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' called ''Shades of Reason'' which first aired in 2013. '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} protocol droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Method ==
Scourge Prime can currently only be obtained from events:

* Scourge Prime could be obtained for free after dealing 240,000 damage against him during the Scoure Boss Fight event.

Scourge Prime will be purchasable at the Nova Shop after the event. He will most likely cost '''100 Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Ability & Trait ==

=== Companion Ability ===
If Scourge Prime is placed in a Protocol Credit Slot, all droids in the selected area (either work/battle/astromech) will generate hive mind credits.

=== Trait: Hive Mind Master ===
Scoure Prime's Iconic Trait is called '''Hive Mind Master'''. This trait adds five effective Hive Mind members while Socurge Prime is working or in a Protocol Credit Slot.

== Income ==
Scourge Prime generates '''15%''' of the players total base income.

== Basis ==
[[File:Scourge Prime Basis.webp|thumb|Scourge Prime as seen in-universe.]]
Scourge Prime, also known simply as the Scourge, is a droid in the Star Wars universe. Created through the fusion of an ancient droid intelligence and the Spark Eternal, Scourge Prime became a powerful and malevolent entity with an insatiable hunger for knowledge. Spreading its consciousness across countless droids, it sought to consume the minds of every being in the galaxy and ultimately control the Force itself, before being confronted and destroyed by Ajax Sigma. Scourge Prime first appeared in a comic called ''Revelations'' ''1'' which was published late 2022. For more information about the basis, check this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Scourge page].

== Trivia ==

* If Scourge Prime is placed on a Protocol slot, the slot will turn into his scourge colors.

== Basis ==
[[File:Snow Mouse Basis.png|thumb|A Snow Mouse in-universe.]]
Snow Mouse is a droid in the Star Wars universe. As a relatively new addition to the franchise, information about these droids remains limited. A cold weather variant of the standard MSE-6 repair unit, the Snow Mouse Droid is outfitted with thermal insulation and heavy treaded wheels designed to navigate sub-zero environments, efficiently delivering messages inside Imperial bases on snow worlds like Phostera. The Snow Mouse first appeared in the 2026 movie ''Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu''. 

== Trivia ==

* Snow Mouse is the first Mythic droid in the drodiex.
* A Snow Mouse blueprint could previously be found in the blueprint storage holder within the cantina's SRB area. Added in v1.13, this marked the initial tease of a Mythic droid before the rarirty was officially introduced in v1.19.2. The blueprint was later removed in a unknown update.

[[File:TDA Basis.jpg|thumb|A TDA seen in-universe.]]
TDA is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. In-universe these droids are called the TDA-series droid assistants. The TDA-series was a humanoid protocol droid model designed to handle administrative and support tasks. The TDA-series first appeared in the fifth epiosde of the first season of ''Star Wars Resistance'' called ''The High Tower'' which first aired in 2018.

== Trivia ==

* TDA was seen at the end of the D-O event in a little teaser for protocol droids.
* TDA is the final non Iconic droid in the droidex.

pages.wikitext:
{{PrevNext|currentsize=50px|previmg=IG-11 Marshall Main.png|prev=IG-11 Marshal|prevsize=50px|currentimg=WG-22 Main.png|next=C-3PO|nextimg=C-3PO Main.png|nextsize=50px}}{{Droid Infobox Official|Name=WG-22|rarity=Iconic|class=Battle|companion_ability=2x Flawless Chance|released=v1.34 (10/10/2026)|image1=WG-22 Main.png}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an {{Official:Rarity|Iconic}} battle droid in Droid Tycoon.

== Obtaining Method ==
{{PAGENAME}} could be obtained during events and can now be obtained at the Nova Shop.

* {{PAGENAME}} could be obtained for free after obtaining 200 Gonk Points during the Iconic Gonk event.
* {{PAGENAME}} will evantually be purchaseable at the Nova Shop for '''Nova Crystals'''.

== Companion Perk & Trait ==
Once WG-22 is set as your companion, every droid you craft has a '''double chance''' of being Flawless. Note that WG-22 must be your active companion when the droid is completed. This bonus also stacks if both the double Flawless chance and a Flawless Charm are active.

=== Trait: Flawless Duplicator ===
''<small>Iconic Traits will not reset after a Super Rebirth.</small>''

WG-22's iconic trait is called '''Flawless Duplicator'''. If WG-22 is equipped as companion, you will be rewarded a blueprint after crafting a flawless event. 

== Income ==
{{PAGENAME}} generates '''15%''' of the players total base income. 

== In-Universe ==
[[File:WG-22 Basis.webp|thumb|WG-22 as seen in-universe.]]
WG-22 is a droid in the Star Wars Universe. WG-22 was a modified power droid that was made to be a gladiator droid to fight in his droid fighting pits inside Fort Ypso on Vandor. The droid's mechanical limbs could puncture metal with devastating might powered by electricity produced in his interior power cells. WG-22 first appeared in the 2018 movie ''Solo: A Star Wars Story''. For more information about WG-22, check out this [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/WG-22 page].

== Trivia ==

* WG-22 was the only new gonk droid added in v1.34 that was classed as a battle droid.
